8. The Applications stand disposed of.
MAC.APP. 418/2025 & CM Appl.39813/2025[Stay]

9. The present Appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [hereinafter referred to as "MV Act"] impugning the award dated 02.04.2025 passed by the learned Presiding Officer, MACT-01, Shahdara Karkardooma Courts, Delhi [hereinafter referred to as "Impugned Award"].

By the Impugned Award, the compensation in the sum of Rs. 28,04,121/- along with interest @ 6% p.a. has been granted to Respondent No.1.
10.
The challenge in the present Appeal is by the owner of the vehicle.
The principal ground of challenge is that the owner has been wrongly implicated.

It is the case of the Appellant that the owner is not aware who the driver was and that the vehicle was not moving but was stationary being parked under a flyover, hence was not involved in the accident.
11.

Learned Counsel for the Appellant relies on the FIR as well as on the evidence of the eye witness to submit that as per the testimony of the eye witness, the front wheel of the rear side of the truck was over the motorcycle and rider of the said motorcycle with his lower limbs was under the motorcycle.
He submits that since this is the description of the accident, the deceased would not have only suffered 35% injuries in his leg but the injury would have been substantially more.
Secondly, he submits that this is also borne from the FIR.
This is a digitally signed order.

The submissions made by the learned Counsel for the Appellant before this Court were also made before the learned Tribunal.
The learned Tribunal gave its finding after a detailed examination, that the testimony of the Appellant does not inspire any confidence.
It was held that the Appellant has stated that the she, despite being the owner of the vehicle did not know who the driver of the vehicle was.
However, it has not been denied that the vehicle was in the custody of the driver at the time of the accident.
Secondly, the learned Tribunal has found that the Appellant has not stated that the driver was not her employee or that the truck had been stolen.
The learned Tribunal has also found that the Appellant was unable to show as to where the offending truck was parked.
12.1 It is apposite to set out paragraphs 17 and 18 of the Impugned Award in this regard below:

"17. The fact, which is very much apparent and clear from the cross- examination of R2W2 (respondent no.2) is that it is respondent no.2 who on the date of the accident was the owner of the offending vehicle.

As R2W2 stated that the keys of the offending Reshma Bahadur vs Amit Kumar & Anr on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170646511/
2 vehicle were in the possession of R2W2 and that R2W2 did not recognize or did not know the respondent no.1/ driver' of the offending vehicle at the time of the accident,
the logical and obvious case of R2W2 being the owner of the offending vehicle would have been that the offending vehicle was stolen.

sentences.text: But, in spite of R2W2 visiting the Police Station Sector-34, Noida, obviously being informed of the accident did not lodge any complaint regarding the theft of the offending vehicle.

Not only that, R2W2 never protested either before the Investigating Officer or any superior officer the police that respondent no. 1 was not her driver, then how from the parking place (wherever that might have been) where the offending vehicle was parked for a couple of years, had been falsely shown by the petitioner/ police officials to be involved in an accident.

18. The deposition of R2W2 in her examination-in-chief as well as cross- examination does not inspire any confidence at all because, in her cross- examination, she was unable to state the exact place where after 2016 the offending truck was parked and she just stated that the driver might have parked it near Mahamaya Flyover.

Further,
she was unable to disclose if, with respect to the parking, any parking charges were paid.
R2W2 stated that she did not pay any parking charges to anybody for parking the

More importantly, how the offending vehicle came at the spot of the accident and from there how the same was found in the police station Sector 34, Naida.

And why, in spite of her vehicle seized by the Investigating Officer being involved in the accident who got it released on superdari and how come R2W2 does not know where the said vehicle is in spite of being its owner when it is the case property of the criminal case and could have been disposed of only by the order of the Criminal Court.

The fact of R2W2 visiting the Hospital to meet the petitioner in spite of the fact that it could have been at the instance of the Investigating Officer of the criminal case indicates that her vehicle i.e.
the offending vehicle, was, in fact, involved in the accident and, in all probability, the same was being driven by the respondent no. l at the time of the accident."
[Emphasis supplied]
13. The learned Tribunal also found that there is no challenge from the Respondent No. 2/driver of the vehicle to the version of the Petitioner since the driver did not step into the witness box.

Thus,
the learned Tribunal found that the rash and negligent driving was proved and since there was no insurance available for the truck, the liability was fastened on the owner of the vehicle, the Appellant.
14. Learned Counsel for the Appellant submits that the finding of the learned Tribunal is not borne from the record.

Learned Counsel seeks to rely upon the FIR, which was registered as well as the Reshma Bahadur vs Amit Kumar & Anr on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170646511/
3 evidence of eye-witness in this regard.

On steps being taken, let Notice be issued to the Respondents via all modes.

In the event, there is any default in depositing the amount, the interim protection granted by this Court shall automatically stand vacated.
